children: UPS said it's rejiggering its operating model in a move aimed at taking advantage of its global footprint.

The company also shook up its executive roles, naming its president of U.S. operations to lead its global operations, as part of the new model. It also disclosed the upcoming retirement of Kate Gutmann, its president, international, healthcare and supply chain solutions.

Under the new model, UPS said it plans to standardize key operational processes across geographies while remaining flexible to meet the needs of local markets. The model is part of UPS's work to evolve into an integrated logistics solutions provider from a small package carrier, the company said.
"At UPS, we intend to leverage the full power of our global network," Chief Executive Carol Tomé said.
Nando Cesarone, currently president of UPS's U.S. operations, will lead the new model as chief global operations officer, the company said.

Cesarone will oversee areas like UPS's global air network and gateways, surface transportation, building and engineering operations, automotive operations and sustainability functions, and report directly to Tomé, UPS said.
The company also named Matt Guffey as chief U.S. domestic officer, with responsibility for its U.S. businesses including small package, Roadie, Happy Returns and UPS Stores.

UPS said it is also searching for an executive to take on its newly created role of chief global commercial strategy officer. The position will be responsible for global strategy, marketing and communications, product management, and pricing.

UPS also said Gutmann will retire from her role for personal family reasons, effective Sept. 1, after more than three decades with the company. Gutmann will remain as an adviser through March 2027, the company said.
UPS veteran Wilfredo Ramos will succeed Gutmann, and report to Tomé. Ramos currently leads UPS's Asia Pacific and brokerage businesses and has worked at the company for more than two decades.
